messages.subject: Re: Deducer/JGR Error
parts:
Hi Tom,

After switching to Yosemite I installed the latest version of Java (version 8, Update 25), which I thought would solve the problem.

I don't understand the remaining part of the instructions link that you sent (http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-patched/R-admin.html#Yosemite). 

Could you explain them to a non-expert like myself? 

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
If needed, set the environment variable JAVA_HOME to choose between these, both when R is built from the sources and when R CMD javareconf is run.

Configuring and building R both looks for a JRE and for support for compiling JNI programs (used by packages rJava andJavaGD); the latter requires a JDK (Java SDK) and not just a JRE.

The build process tries to fathom out what JRE/JDK to use, but it may need some help, e.g. by setting JAVA_HOME. The Apple JRE can be specified explicitly by something like

JAVA_HOME=/System/Library/Frameworks/JavaVM.framework/Home
JAVA_CPPFLAGS="-I/System/Library/Frameworks/JavaVM.framework/Headers"
JAVA_LD_LIBRARY_PATH=
JAVA_LIBS="-framework JavaVM"

The Apple developer versions of the JDK install somewhere like

JAVA_HOME=/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/1.6.0_43-b01-447.jdk/Contents/Home

The Oracle JDK can be specified explicitly by something like

JAVA_HOME=/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk1.8.0_25.jdk/Contents/Home
JAVA_CPPFLAGS="-I/${JAVA_HOME}/include -I/${JAVA_HOME}/include/darwin"
JAVA_LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${JAVA_HOME}/jre/lib/server"
JAVA_LIBS="-L/${JAVA_HOME}/jre/lib/server -ljvm"

in config.site.

Note that it is necessary to set the environment variable NOAWT to 1 to install many of the Java-using packages.

messages.subject: Re: Deducer/JGR Error
parts:
If you are able to load JGR, none of those instructions are relevant. It is possible you have something very funky hanging around in your workspace. try:

rm(list=ls())
q(save="yes”)

which will remove all objects from your workspace, save it and quit. Note that this will delete any objects you have in your current default workspace, so make sure you don’t have any unsaved critical data there (which you really shouldn’t).

Ian

messages.author: 1e82ea932416652e
messages.subject: Re: Deducer/JGR Error
parts:
Roger,

From other threads in r-sig-mac and elsewhere, it looks like you need Apple's Java from http://support.apple.com/kb/DL1572.The Oracle version seems to have some issues. If you use Apple's Java, you probably won't need to worry about setting the JAVA_HOME environment variable. The rest of the instructions under the "Yosemite" section are to reinstall XQuartz and the XCode command-line tools, and to follow the directions for upgrading to Mavericks (the previous section of the document), which is, I think, just instructions for settings in config.site if compilation of source files fails. Hopefully you won't have to worry about that part.

Regards,

Tom

Sent from my iPhone

On Nov 20, 2014, at 4:37 PM, Roger Taylor <roger...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Tom,

After switching to Yosemite I installed the latest version of Java (version 8, Update 25), which I thought would solve the problem.

I don't understand the remaining part of the instructions link that you sent (http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-patched/R-admin.html#Yosemite). 

Could you explain them to a non-expert like myself? 

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
If needed, set the environment variable JAVA_HOME to choose between these, both when R is built from the sources and when R CMD javareconf is run.

Configuring and building R both looks for a JRE and for support for compiling JNI programs (used by packages rJava andJavaGD); the latter requires a JDK (Java SDK) and not just a JRE.

The build process tries to fathom out what JRE/JDK to use, but it may need some help, e.g. by setting JAVA_HOME. The Apple JRE can be specified explicitly by something like

JAVA_HOME=/System/Library/Frameworks/JavaVM.framework/Home
JAVA_CPPFLAGS="-I/System/Library/Frameworks/JavaVM.framework/Headers"
JAVA_LD_LIBRARY_PATH=
JAVA_LIBS="-framework JavaVM"

The Apple developer versions of the JDK install somewhere like

JAVA_HOME=/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/1.6.0_43-b01-447.jdk/Contents/Home

The Oracle JDK can be specified explicitly by something like

JAVA_HOME=/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk1.8.0_25.jdk/Contents/Home
JAVA_CPPFLAGS="-I/${JAVA_HOME}/include -I/${JAVA_HOME}/include/darwin"
JAVA_LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${JAVA_HOME}/jre/lib/server"
JAVA_LIBS="-L/${JAVA_HOME}/jre/lib/server -ljvm"

in config.site.

Note that it is necessary to set the environment variable NOAWT to 1 to install many of the Java-using packages.

On Nov 20, 2014, at 4:37 PM, Roger Taylor <roger...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Tom,

After switching to Yosemite I installed the latest version of Java (version 8, Update 25), which I thought would solve the problem.

I don't understand the remaining part of the instructions link that you sent (http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-patched/R-admin.html#Yosemite). 

Could you explain them to a non-expert like myself? 

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
If needed, set the environment variable JAVA_HOME to choose between these, both when R is built from the sources and when R CMD javareconf is run.

Configuring and building R both looks for a JRE and for support for compiling JNI programs (used by packages rJava andJavaGD); the latter requires a JDK (Java SDK) and not just a JRE.

The build process tries to fathom out what JRE/JDK to use, but it may need some help, e.g. by setting JAVA_HOME. The Apple JRE can be specified explicitly by something like

JAVA_HOME=/System/Library/Frameworks/JavaVM.framework/Home
JAVA_CPPFLAGS="-I/System/Library/Frameworks/JavaVM.framework/Headers"
JAVA_LD_LIBRARY_PATH=
JAVA_LIBS="-framework JavaVM"

The Apple developer versions of the JDK install somewhere like

JAVA_HOME=/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/1.6.0_43-b01-447.jdk/Contents/Home

The Oracle JDK can be specified explicitly by something like

JAVA_HOME=/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk1.8.0_25.jdk/Contents/Home
JAVA_CPPFLAGS="-I/${JAVA_HOME}/include -I/${JAVA_HOME}/include/darwin"
JAVA_LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${JAVA_HOME}/jre/lib/server"
JAVA_LIBS="-L/${JAVA_HOME}/jre/lib/server -ljvm"

in config.site.

Note that it is necessary to set the environment variable NOAWT to 1 to install many of the Java-using packages.
